samples.text: In floating‑point arithmetic each operation rounds the exact real result to the nearest representable value because numbers are stored with a finite number of bits. This rounding can change the magnitude of intermediate results, so adding a tiny number to a large one may be lost, while adding the tiny numbers together first can preserve them. As a result, \((a+b)+c\) and \(a+(b+c)\) can yield different rounded values, demonstrating that floating‑point addition is not associative.
